newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on Tuesday on interbank and retail interest, dealers said.

"The interbank rate slipped slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly higher but bond prices were easier. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from Monday's yield of 2.00/1.95 percent but one-year closed at a yield of 2.27/2.22 percent compared with Monday's yield of 2.20/2.15 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.95/99.00 versus Monday's close of S$99.03/99.08, May 2002 at S$99.88/99.93 against S$99.90/99.95 and June 2003 at S$94.95/95.00 from S$94.98/95.03.
The overnight interbank offered rate slipped to 1-5/8 1-1/2 percent versus Monday's 2 1-7/8 percent.
